title: Retire six writing rules into unplaceable-reference
summary: Six writing rules — bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name and undefined-name-at-start — are deleted and their coverage folded into the single unplaceable-reference rule. Because those ids can still appear in config files, suppression markers, osf-expect declarations and `osf explain` invocations, the change threads a RETIRED_RULE_IDS table through the config loader, the suppression engine, the expectation checker and the CLI so every stale mention fails loudly and names its replacement instead of silently doing nothing.

lanes.label: CLI surface
lanes.subtitle: osf binary
lanes.summary: The commands a user or agent runs: lint, verify, explain, and the config loader they all share.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: osf-lint-core crate
lanes.summary: Rule-agnostic machinery: suppression markers, expectation checking, and the human/SARIF renderers.

lanes.label: Writing rules
lanes.subtitle: osf::lints::writing
lanes.summary: The rule set itself, now collapsed onto one reference-and-name rule, plus the retired-id table that names replacements.

lanes.label: Agent integrations
lanes.subtitle: dsh, omp, opencode
lanes.summary: Adapters that read osf's exit code and decision JSON; they only observe rule ids in the text they pass through.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: main.rs
nodes.summary: Entry point. `explain` now short-circuits on a retired id and prints the replacement instead of the bare 'no such rule' error; `expectation_findings` emits a new expectation-retired-rule finding.

nodes.label: Config loader
nodes.subtitle: config.rs
nodes.summary: Drops the chat_local_labels field and its env var, rewrites the deny_unknown_fields message for that key, and rejects any writing.levels entry keyed by a retired rule id.

nodes.label: verify stage
nodes.subtitle: verify.rs
nodes.summary: Pre-commit and pre-push fixture checking; passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS into the expectation check and turns retired declarations into expectation-retired-rule findings.

nodes.label: RETIRED_RULE_IDS
nodes.subtitle: &[(&str, &str)]
nodes.summary: The single source of truth: six old ids each paired with unplaceable-reference. Read by the config loader, the suppression engine, the expectation checker and `osf explain`.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: No longer calls undefined_names; passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS to apply_suppressions; apply_context now resolves every rule from the finding's own evidence rather than special-casing unplaceable-reference.

nodes.label: unplaceable-reference
nodes.subtitle: the surviving rule
nodes.summary: The one rule that now covers bare numbers, unlabelled references, unlinked references, chat-local phrases and labels, and unexplained names. Its metadata is the only reference/name entry left in RULE_META.

nodes.label: six retired rules
nodes.subtitle: bare-reference, reference-without-*, chat-local-reference, undefined-name*
nodes.summary: Deleted rule functions, their RULE_META entries, their fixture pairs, and the chat_local_labels config field that fed chat-local-reference.

nodes.label: apply_suppressions
nodes.subtitle: suppress.rs
nodes.summary: Takes a retired_rules slice; an unknown id found there still errors as suppression-unknown-rule but the message says it was replaced and names the replacement.

nodes.label: check_expectation
nodes.subtitle: expectation.rs
nodes.summary: Mismatch gains a retired list. A declared id naming a retired rule is reported there with its replacement, is never folded into missing, and its replacement firing is not also reported as unexpected.

nodes.label: human / SARIF renderers
nodes.subtitle: human.rs, sarif.rs
nodes.summary: Unchanged behaviour; only their test fixtures swap bare-reference for unplaceable-reference.

nodes.label: agent adapters
nodes.subtitle: dsh, omp, opencode
nodes.summary: Read osf's exit code and decision JSON. They only see rule ids inside the reason string, so their tests move to unplaceable-reference with no logic change.

edges.label: load config
edges.summary: Every command loads config first; the loader now refuses retired level keys and the removed chat_local_labels key.

edges.label: explain <retired id>
edges.summary: `osf explain bare-reference` now reads the retired table and prints the replacement, exiting 0 instead of 2.

edges.label: passes retired ids
edges.summary: lint_writing hands the retired table to the suppression engine so stale markers get a useful message.

edges.label: no longer runs
edges.summary: undefined_names and the chat-local rule are gone from the rule list; the six ids no longer fire.

edges.label: reject_retired_levels
edges.summary: A writing.levels key naming a retired rule is an error naming unplaceable-reference.

flows.title: A stale retired id is refused and redirected
flows.summary: What happens when a config file, suppression marker, fixture declaration or `osf explain` call still names one of the six deleted rules.

messages.label: ('undefined-name-at-start', 'unplaceable-reference')
messages.note: A hit becomes an error: "the rule 'undefined-name-at-start' is gone; use 'writing.levels.unplaceable-reference' instead".

messages.label: ('bare-reference', 'unplaceable-reference')
messages.note: Still a suppression-unknown-rule error, but the message says the id was replaced and names the replacement.

messages.label: Mismatch { missing, unexpected, retired }
messages.note: A retired declaration is never counted as missing, and its replacement firing is not counted as unexpected.

messages.label: "'bare-reference' is not a rule id any more; it was replaced by 'unplaceable-reference'"
messages.note: Exit code 0, not the old 2 — the id is recognised, just retired.

views.title: Retired-id redirection across the toolchain
views.summary: The six deleted rules leave a trail of stale ids in config files, suppression markers, fixture declarations and CLI calls. RETIRED_RULE_IDS is the one table every consumer reads to turn those into a message naming unplaceable-reference.

views.title: Writing rule set after the collapse
views.summary: Inside the writing lint: the six old rule functions and their metadata are gone, and unplaceable-reference is the only reference-and-name rule left.

views.title: Lint core plumbing
views.summary: The rule-agnostic layer: suppression markers and expectation checking both gained a retired-id parameter, while the human and SARIF renderers are untouched.
